podcast.title: Self-Isolation and Depression (1998-1999)
podcast.body: In February 1998, after completing his studies at Harvard, Rivers Cuomo moved back to LA and into an apartment under a freeway in Culver City. Still hurt by "Pinkerton"'s poor reception, he sought self-isolation, unplugging his phone, sealing all light by covering windows with fiberglass insulation, painting the walls black for ultimate darkness, and only communicating with his pet gecko for a year. He was very depressed and without a car, became immobile in Los Angeles. "Rivers was very depressed. He didn't own a car either."

podcast.title: Responsive to Fan Request (2018)
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo, frontman of Weezer, famously responded to a tweet from a 14-year-old fan who requested the band cover Toto's "Africa," leading to the recording of the song, which became Weezer's biggest rock radio hit in a decade. "a 14-year-old Weaser fan tweeted at Frontman Rivers Cuomo that the band should record Africa."

podcast.title: Aversion to Punk Funk
podcast.body: In the early 90s, Rivers Cuomo was talked out of forming a punk funk band because he worried it would hinder the band's chances, especially with the growing emphasis on authenticity in the alternative scene. As a former metalhead, he feared this background could be detrimental to the group. "Rivers had been talked out of forming a punk funk band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Birth and Childhood
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo was born in New York City to a hippie musician father and a hippie mother. He was raised in several Buddhist communities for the first ten years of his life, including an ashram called Yogaville, before his parents divorced in 1975, and the family settled in Connecticut. "Rivers was born in New York City. Dad was a hippie musician, and mum was a hippie hippie hippie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Confessional Lyrical Style
podcast.body: As the singer for Weezer, Rivers Cuomo was known for his highly confessional lyrics, which frequently expressed themes of fear, bitterness, and confusion. This introspective lyrical approach resonated strongly with emo fans. "Singer Rivers Cuomo was a fan of highly confessional lyrics, expressing fear and bitterness and confusion. Again, emo fans gravitated to River's Cuomo's headspace."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 3: Emo

podcast.title: Desire for a Weezer Movie
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo harbors a long-term goal to create a Weezer movie, not just a tour film, but an actual cinematic production. "And one day he wants to make a Weezer movie, not a tour film, but some kind of actual movie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Disillusionment with Rock Star Lifestyle
podcast.body: The creation of "Pinkerton" reflected Rivers Cuomo's deep disillusionment with the rock star lifestyle, which contributed to the album's darker themes. "Pinkerton was...darker and reflected Rivers' disillusionment with the rock star lifestyle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Diverse Interests
podcast.body: Beyond music, Rivers Cuomo is an avid pickleball player, a very good chess player, and is deeply fascinated with Japanese culture. "River's has also taken a pickleball with a vengeance. He's a very good chess player, and he's fascinated with Japanese culture."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Harvard TV Show "The Pilot"
podcast.body: A film called "The Pilot" for a TV show was based on the period when Rivers Cuomo attended Harvard University. "This film, The Pilot, for a TV show based on the year's Rivers Went to Harvard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Harvard University Enrollment (First Time)
podcast.body: In September 1995, while still healing from his leg surgery and walking with a cane, Rivers Cuomo enrolled at Harvard University to study classical composition. His studies consumed a lot of his time, impacting his songwriting. He tried out for a Harvard choir but did not make it and kept to himself, growing a beard. He found it amusing that classmates wearing Weezer T-shirts had no idea he was Rivers Cuomo. "In September 1995, still healing and walking with a cane, Rivers enrolled at Harvard University to study classical composition."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Harvard University Enrollment (Second Time)
podcast.body: After Weezer's break following the "Pinkerton" tour, Rivers Cuomo returned to Harvard, completing semesters in 1997 and 1998. During this time, he played in a campus band called Homey. "Rivers went back to Harvard, completing semesters in 1997 and 1998."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Japanese Culture and Fuji Rock Festival
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo's long-standing interest in Japanese culture, combined with an invitation to perform at the Fuji Rock Festival in Japan, rekindled the band's excitement for making music after a hiatus. "Rivers, Spanish Japan, okay? And that got them excited about making music again."

podcast.title: Knitting Hobby
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo enjoys knitting as a hobby to relax. "River's Cuomo likes to knit."

podcast.title: Kurt Cobain Identical Theory
podcast.body: A Reddit-born theory claims Rivers Cuomo and Kurt Cobain are the same person, suggesting Cobain is not dead. The theory cites Weezer's "Goat Punishment" secret show in November 1998, where they performed six Nirvana songs (e.g., "Swapmate," "Aneurysm"). Other points include shared biographer John D. Luerssen, both bands being on the same label, and Weezer touring with Foo Fighters. It also noted no conflicting tour or studio schedules between the bands, implying a potential hidden identity. "The existence of that recording is enough to convince some people that Rivers Cuomo and Kurt Cobain are actually the same person."

srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

podcast.title: Lack of a Middle Name
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo does not have a middle name because his parents intended for him to choose one when he was old enough, but he never got around to it. "He doesn't have a middle name because his parents wanted him to choose one when he got old enough, but he just never got around to it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Leg Injury's Impact on Guitar Playing
podcast.body: His leg injury significantly affected Rivers Cuomo's guitar playing, as he couldn't stretch his leg out. This constraint forced him to write most of the songs on the "Pinkerton" album with limited mobility on the fretboard. "His leg affected his guitar playing too. He couldn't stretch it out so he had to write most of the songs on the album with limited mobility on the fretboard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Leg Lengthening Surgery
podcast.body: Born with his right leg 44 millimeters (1.75 inches) shorter than his left, Rivers Cuomo underwent expensive and painful leg lengthening surgery in March 1995, funded by earnings from "The Blue Album." The procedure involved breaking the bone, fixing it with a brace, and gradually stretching it with screws over months, causing significant pain and affecting his mental state and songwriting for the second album. "But as he grew, his right one grew to be 44 millimeters, one and three quarter inches shorter than his left."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Origin of His Name "Rivers"
podcast.body: There are two stories about his name. One states his father, a soccer fan, named him after three players from the 1970 World Cup (Revilino of Brazil, Luigi Riva, and Gianni Rivera of Italy). The other story attributes it to his birth in a hospital between the East and Hudson Rivers in New York City, with his mother reportedly hearing one of the rivers outside her window. "Well, there were two stories."

podcast.title: PETA's Sexiest Celebrity Vegetarian
podcast.body: PETA once voted Rivers Cuomo the sexiest celebrity vegetarian, though he personally confesses to hating carrots. "Pita once voted him the sexiest celebrity vegetarian, although he does confess to hating carrots."

podcast.title: Pet Squirrel Mr. Peanut Butter
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo once had a pet squirrel named Mr. Peanut Butter. "And once he had a pet squirrel named Mr. Peanut Butter."

podcast.title: Post-Pinkerton Isolation and Songwriting Plan
podcast.body: Following the underperformance of Weezer's second album, *Pinkerton*, Rivers Cuomo withdrew from Harvard, where he was studying music. He secluded himself in a room painted entirely black and insulated the windows, intending to purge all weaknesses and dedicate himself to crafting the "perfect pop song." "When Weezer's second album, Pinkerton, didn't do as well as Rivers Quomo had hoped, he dropped out of Harvard where he had been studying music and hid in his room, which are the walls and ceilings painted black and had the windows blacked out with layers of fiberglass insulation. The plan was to purge himself of all weaknesses so we could concentrate on writing the perfect pop song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 60 Minutes: 2017 Edition

podcast.title: Productivity During Isolation
podcast.body: Despite his severe depression and self-isolation in a blacked-out apartment under a freeway, Rivers Cuomo was incredibly productive, writing 121 songs during this period. Some of these songs were later released as part of the "Alone, the Home Recordings of Rivers Cuomo" series. "In that blacked out apartment, under the freeway, he wrote 121 songs."

podcast.title: Roadie for King's Eyes
podcast.body: For a period, Rivers Cuomo worked as a roadie for a band called King's Eyes, alongside his college enrollment and music writing. "He also, for a while worked as a roadie for a band called King's Eyes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stage Entrance Method
podcast.body: There was a story about Rivers Cuomo of Weezer entering venues undetected by fans by climbing into a wheelie bin or road case after exiting the tour bus. Roadies would then push him to the stage, keeping him out of sight. "He'd exit the tour bus, climb into some kind of wheelie bin, maybe a road case, and then be pushed undetected by roadies to wherever he needed to be out of sight of fans."

podcast.title: Stepfather Stephen Kits
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo gained a stepfather named Stephen Kits when his family lived in the Yogaville ashram. "This is where Rivers gained a stepfather named Stephen Kits."

podcast.title: Temporary Name Change to Peter Kits
podcast.body: For a couple of years in the mid-1980s, Rivers Cuomo changed his name to Peter Kits. This name appeared in one of his very first bands, a glammy metal group called Among Guard, before he reverted to Rivers. "He also, for a time, changed his name to Peter Kits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tower Records Employment and Influences
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo had a part-time job at the famous Tower Records on Sunset Boulevard, which was crucial as Alt Rock was emerging. This exposed him to bands like Pixies, Nirvana, Sonic Youth, and Nine Inch Nails, and also led him to meet drummer Patrick Wilson, who would become a Weezer member. "Working in the record store exposed him to the pixies and Nirvana, Sonic Youth, and Nine Inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unlikely Rock Star Persona
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo is described as an "unlikely sort of rock star," committed to maintaining his status. He is highly educated, deeply introspective, very private, and constantly seeking to learn new things, from songwriting to computer programming, intense meditation, and music industry studies. "If Forever's Cuomo of Weezer were to walk past you on the street, you probably wouldn't notice him."

xref.title: Return from Hiatus (2000)
xref.body: Weezer participated in the Warped Tour in 2000, which served as their method for easing back into performing after a hiatus. This break occurred between their _Pinkerton_ album in 1996 and the _Green Album_ in 2001, during which Rivers Cuomo attended Harvard. "Warped was their way of easing themselves back into the game after Rivers Cuomo took time to go to Harvard."

xref.title: Archetypical Nerd Rock Band
xref.body: Weezer is considered the ultimate nerd rock band, characterized by the quirky and bookish personality of its leader, Rivers Cuomo, who is described as neurotic and socially awkward. Their platinum records towards the end of the 1990s helped solidify the genre's presence and inspire more nerd rock bands. "We talked about them as the archetypical nerd rock band off the top of the show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Nerd Rock

xref.title: Band's Collective Songwriting on Red Album
xref.body: For the Red Album, Pat Wilson, Brian Bell, and Scott Shriner also contributed songs, marking a more collaborative songwriting effort beyond Rivers Cuomo's primary role. Scott Shriner described his musical contributions as "just based on feeling," with Rivers often writing the lyrics. "Pat Brian and Scott wrote songs in this album too, so I can't speak for them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Black Album Delay
xref.body: The Black Album was initially planned to follow the White Album, intended to be a darker counterpart. However, the songs Rivers Cuomo developed were not dark enough, leading to the Black Album being put on hold. What was released instead was Pacific Daydream. "So they had no choice but to put the Black Album on hold."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Black Hole Sessions Repurposing
xref.body: Although *Songs from the Black Hole* was never officially released, many recordings from these sessions were repurposed for other albums, released in different forms, or appeared on Rivers Cuomo's solo recordings *Alone, the Home Recordings of Rivers Cuomo* (Volumes 1 and 2). "However, there were plenty of recordings floating about from the Black Hole sessions. Some of the songs were repurposed or released in other forms and other albums, and Rivers released a bunch of this material on two volumes of solo recordings called Alone, the Home Recordings of Rivers Cuomo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bus Accident on Ratitude Tour
xref.body: On December 6, 2009, while on tour for the "Ratitude" album, Weezer's bus hit a patch of ice on the New York State Thruway near Glen. The bus went over the median, hit posts, crossed the highway again, jumped a guard rail, and landed in a ditch. Rivers Cuomo, his wife Kyoko, daughter Mia, nanny, and assistant Sarah were on board. Rivers sustained three cracked ribs and internal bleeding, leading to the cancellation of the remaining tour dates. "On December 6th, 2009, Weezer was on tour for the Ratitude album."

xref.title: Computer Program for Teal Album Covers Selection
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo wrote a computer program that analyzed Spotify data to select songs for the Teal Album. The program identified popular songs not tagged as Alt Rock or Classic Rock and narrowed the list to those released before 1994, generating 200 titles for the band to consider. "Rivers wrote a computer program that sucked in all kinds of Spotify data."

xref.title: Extensive Demos and Unreleased Material
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo has an immense catalog of demos, possibly thousands, some dating back as far as 1979, which he has posted online or released on compilations. This extensive archive provides numerous "rabbit holes" for fans to explore. "There are hundreds, well, probably thousands, literally thousands, of demos that Rivers Cuomo has either posted online or released on compilations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: External Collaborators and Multiple Producers for Ratitude
xref.body: For "Ratitude," Weezer brought in outside collaborators for the first time, including Jermaine Dupri, members of All-American Rejects, Lil Wayne, Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic, and the guys from Sloan (though uncredited and parts recorded in 2003). The album also had four producers, including Dr. Luke and Jacknife Lee, plus Rivers Cuomo, totaling five. "For the first time outside collaborators were brought in, including Germain Dupree, a couple of guys from all American rejects, Lil Wayne, Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic, and the guys from Sloan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Fan Collaboration for "Turning Up the Radio"
xref.body: The project "Let's Write a Song" (SAWNG) for the track "Turning Up the Radio" involved fans submitting ideas for song titles, chord progressions, lyrics, and melodies through YouTube videos. This highly creative and interactive project utilized the ideas of 16 different fans, alongside Rivers Cuomo's contributions, for the final song on "Death to False Metal." "The project was called Let's Write a Song, and song is spelled S-A-W-N-G in this particular case."

xref.title: First Gig and Band Naming
xref.body: The band's first offer to play came on March 19, 1992, at a club called Rodgies, headlining Dog Star, which featured Keanu Reeves on bass. Needing a proper permanent name for the gig, Rivers Cuomo, Patrick Wilson, Jason Cropper, and Matt Sharp chose "Weezer," a nickname Rivers had been given by his father, referencing a character in "The Little Rascals." "And eventually Rivers, Pat, Jason, and bass player Matt Sharp now went with the name Weezer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

xref.title: Harvard Enrollment Impact
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo's enrollment at Harvard in the fall of 1995 contributed to the abandonment of the *Songs from the Black Hole* project, as he "didn't really have any time for this rock and roll silliness anymore." "Rivers had enrolled at Harvard and didn't really have any time for this rock and roll silliness anymore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Lost Albums

xref.title: Hurley Album Cover Model
xref.body: Jorge Garcia, who played the character Hurley in the TV series "Lost," is featured on the cover of Weezer's "Hurley" album. The image is a cropped picture of Rivers Cuomo hugging Garcia in the green room of the late-night talk show "Lopez Tonight," where both were guests. "That's Jorge Garcia, a guy you played early on the show on the cover."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Inspiration for Weezer Song
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo of Weezer saw pictures of the girl group Wilson Phillips in a program at the opening of a new phase of the Hollywood Bowl, which inspired him to think about what it would be like to marry an established, successful celebrity, leading to the song "Beverly Hills." "Fliving through the program, he saw pictures of the girl group Wilson Phillips."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Journal and Spreadsheet for Lyrics
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo stored vocal thoughts in a journal, selecting the best bits to transfer to a spreadsheet. This spreadsheet was organized by the number of syllables in each line and by "strong weak emphasis," a concept likely learned from his English degree. He then ordered the data to fit melodies and tell stories. "Vocal thoughts were stored in a journal with the best bits making it onto a spreadsheet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Nerd Rock Persona
xref.body: Weezer is considered the "ultimate nerd rock band of all time," largely due to the quirky, bookish, neurotic, and socially awkward personality of its leader, Rivers Cuomo, combined with the often self-referential and meme-laden content of their music videos. "we have a primo nerd rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Nerd Rock

xref.title: Personal Tragedies and Birth of Son Leo
xref.body: After the bus accident, Rivers Cuomo experienced further personal challenges, including the death of former bassist Mikey Welsh from an overdose in a Chicago hotel room on October 8, 2011. He also lost his grandfather, a former girlfriend, and his meditation teacher. In 2012, Rivers and Kyoko had a son, Leo, whose birth was difficult. These events prompted Rivers to seek a slower pace after a period of prolific releases. "On October 8th, 2011, former bass player Mikey Welsh was found dead of an overdose in a Chicago hotel room."

xref.title: Post-Make Believe Breakup Rumors
xref.body: After the "Make Believe" album cycle, rumors circulated that Weezer was breaking up. This was fueled by Rivers Cuomo returning to Harvard, his marriage, and other band members focusing on side projects, along with Rivers' own quote in an interview suggesting the band was "done for the moment." "However, after this album cycle was completed, there were rumors that Weezer was breaking up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Producer Ric Ocasek's Persuasion
xref.body: Despite Rivers Cuomo's strong reservations, producer Ric Ocasek, leader of The Cars, was adamant about including "Buddy Holly" on the debut album. He, along with the other band members, insisted on its inclusion. Ocasek eventually convinced Cuomo by suggesting they record it, and if Cuomo still disliked it, they could leave it off, but warning him it would be "stupid not to include it." "But Rico Kasek, the leader of the cars and the guy tapped to produce the record, would have none of that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stories Behind Songs - 5

xref.title: Programmers for Pacific Daydream Spreadsheet
xref.body: For the Pacific Daydream album, Rivers Cuomo hired programmers to organize his songwriting data in an even more granular way. They tagged everything with specific attributes, and one tab in his spreadsheet contained about 5,500 "cool" lyrical fragments, which he used when stuck for inspiration. The programmers used Python for this task. "During this time, he hired some programmers to organize the data in an even more granular way, tagging everything with specific attributes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Ritalin and Tequila Songwriting Experiments
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo's creative process for some songs, including "Hashpipe" and "Dope Nose," involved unusual experiments he called his "catalog of riffs." These entailed plugging in a guitar, taking one Ritalin pill with three shots of tequila, going into the backyard, and sometimes closing his eyes to see if songs appeared in his mind. "The creation of a lot of this material involved plugging in a guitar, taking one riddle in pill with three shots of tequila and then going out into the backyard to see what happened."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Riverpedia / The Library / Drive Times App
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo created something called the "Riverpedia," now known as "The Library," which began as a homework assignment and was posted online on August 18, 2020. This evolved into an app called "Drive Times," designed to automate tour logistics like scheduling venue arrivals, road travel, and private plane flights. He learned to code in Python during the pandemic lockdown to create this. "He created something called the Riverpedia, which is now known as the Library."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo Identical Theory
xref.body: A theory, which originated on Reddit, claims that Kurt Cobain and Rivers Cuomo of Weezer are the same person, suggesting Kurt did not die. Proponents point to a November 1998 "Goat Punishment" secret show where Weezer played six Nirvana songs, the shared biographer John D. Luerssen, the fact that both bands were signed to the same label, and Weezer having toured with the Foo Fighters. The theory also notes that Nirvana and Weezer's studio and tour dates never conflicted. "The first is that Kurt and River's Cuomo of Weezer are actually the same person."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo as Roadie
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo worked as a roadie for King's Eyes for a period of time, alongside his college studies and musical endeavors. "He also, for a while worked as a roadie for a band called King's Eyes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Coding Skills
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo dedicated part of the pandemic lockdown to learning to code himself, ultimately creating the "Drive Times" app for tour logistics. He achieved a 95 in his coding class and is described as a "pretty fair Python programmer." "In case you're wondering, Rivers got a 95 in his coding class."

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Early Band
xref.body: This was one of Rivers Cuomo's very first bands, a "glammy metal group," where he performed under the name Peter Kits. The band played maybe six shows before Peter reverted to Rivers, and the group moved to Los Angeles, eventually changing their name to Zoom and breaking up in 1990. "They played maybe six shows before Peter reverted to Rivers and the band moved out to Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Experimental Approach to Ratitude
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo embraced an experimental mindset for "Ratitude," telling the band, "this is just one more album out of many more that we're going to make." This indicated a willingness to take risks, suggesting that if an experiment didn't work out, they would simply try something different for the next album. "So in other words, if it works out great, if it doesn't, fine, we'll do something different for the next album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Friendship with King He
xref.body: The song "Buddy Holly" was a direct result of Rivers Cuomo's protectiveness over his Korean friend, King He. Cuomo became "really pissed off" when other band members made fun of her, recalling how she was often picked on in high school. The song was written as an expression of his commitment to their platonic relationship and his readiness to defend her. "It's about a particular girl I knew."

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Harvard Campus Band
xref.body: Homey was a campus band Rivers Cuomo played in during his second stint at Harvard (1997 and 1998). It had a rotating cast of musicians and played a couple of shows. "He played in a campus band called Homey for a while."

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Home Recordings
xref.body: A number of other songs from the aborted *Songs from the Black Hole* project appear on Rivers Cuomo's Home Recordings releases. "If you want to go deeper into this aborted record, a number of other songs from Songs from the Black Hole appear on Rivers Home Recordings releases."

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Initial Rejection of "Buddy Holly"
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo initially refused to consider including "Buddy Holly" on Weezer's debut album, deeming it "too cheesy" and an outlier compared to his other compositions. He felt it didn't fit the band's intended sound. "For the longest time, he refused to consider including the song and Weezer's debut album because it was too cheesy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Meditation Practice (Vipassanā)
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo practices Vipassanā meditation, a Sanskrit term meaning "to see things as they are," which has been around for at least 2,500 years. He practices at least two hours a day. Producer Rick Rubin first suggested it around 2003 when Weezer was working on the Red Album. Rivers initially feared it would rob him of angst but found it enhanced his creativity and made him "10% happier." "It's called Vispasana, that's Sanskrit for to see things as they are."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Metal Band Past
xref.body: The album "Van Weezer" was noted as a return to Rivers Cuomo's musical roots, specifically referencing his past in a metal band before forming Weezer. This informed the heavier sound of the album. "Remember how Rivers was in a metal band before Weezer? This was a return to that time, sort of."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Personal Life & Hiatus
xref.body: Following the "Make Believe" album, Rivers Cuomo returned to Harvard to finish his English degree. He married Kyoko Ito on June 18, 2006, after meeting her in 1997, with a ceremony on a remote beach near Malibu and a honeymoon in Japan. During this period, he made a comment during his honeymoon interview suggesting the band might be "done," which contributed to breakup fears when no new album appeared in 2006 or 2007. "Rivers returned to Harvard to finish his degree in English. He got married to Kyoto, Ito on June 18, 2006."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Pizza Crust Habit
xref.body: During the band's early, poor days, Rivers Cuomo would save pizza crusts in a fanny pack to eat later, demonstrating the band's financial struggles. "They were so poor that Rivers would save pizza crusts in a fanny pack."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Songwriting Inspiration
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo primarily draws inspiration from his own life and feelings, starting with personal experiences and then using "a little artistry" to make the songs more relatable. He confirmed that his songs for this particular album came directly from his life, though he couldn't speak for other band members' contributions. "My favorite source of inspiration is my own life and my own feelings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo's Stream of Consciousness Songwriting
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo generates a vast number of songs by embracing a "stream of consciousness" approach, letting ideas flow freely. While most of these ideas might be discarded, he believes some "gems" will emerge, contributing to his prolific output (e.g., sorting through 250 songs for the White Album, only one making the cut). "Well Rivers says he's all about stream of consciousness. He just lets the ideas flow."

xref.title: Songwriting Process on Santa Monica College Campus
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo developed the lyrics for "Buddy Holly" while walking through the campus of Santa Monica College, where both he and King He were attending school. The iconic line "weew, I look just like Buddy Holly" was conceived at the same speed as his walking pace, indicating an organic, real-time inspiration. "He came up with the lyrics while walking through the campus of Santa Monica College where he and King He were attending school."

xref.title: Spotify Playlists for Chord Progressions
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo developed a unique songwriting process that began with creating Spotify playlists. These playlists featured songs with chord progressions he found interesting, providing a foundation for new melodies. "Rivers began by creating Spotify playlists featuring songs with chord progression that he found interesting."

xref.title: Studio Dynamics and "Buddy Holly" Notes
xref.body: During the recording sessions for Weezer's debut album, notes reading "weew, what, Buddy Holly" began to appear around the studio. This suggests the other band members and producer Ric Ocasek were playfully but persistently advocating for the song's inclusion, despite Rivers Cuomo's initial reluctance. "Little notes started appearing around the studio that said, weew, what, Buddy Holly."

xref.title: Suggested Meditation to Rivers Cuomo
xref.body: Producer Rick Rubin suggested Vipassanā meditation to Rivers Cuomo around 2003, when Weezer was working on the Red Album. Rivers initially resisted but eventually found it beneficial for his creativity and well-being. "It was producer Rick Rubin, who first suggested this in about 2003 when Weezer was working on the red album."

xref.title: Tagged as Emo
xref.body: Weezer, an LA-based band, became associated with the emo label due to their nerdy and geeky image, singer Rivers Cuomo's highly confessional lyrics (expressing fear, bitterness, and confusion), big and loud guitar sounds, and notable punk rock influences. "And one LA band that got tagged with the emo label was Weezer. And you can see why. I mean, they were nerdy and they were geeky."

xref.title: Tinder Account for Songwriting Inspiration
xref.body: For the White Album, Rivers Cuomo signed up for a Tinder account to meet people and then wrote about those experiences. Because he was living in California, these encounters often coalesced into themes related to the beach and ocean, including surfers, beach bums, and specific characters like "Harry Christmas." "Rivers signed up for a Tinder account and he met with people and then wrote about those experiences."

xref.title: Transition from Meditation to Crafts
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo developed an interest in knitting after getting into meditation in the mid-2000s. This led him to also explore clay sculptures and whittling. He used to knit in bed while his wife read Sherlock Holmes mysteries, though he now states he has less time for it due to his work commitments. "Things began when he got into meditation in the mid-Auts."

xref.title: Unofficial Album Leak
xref.body: In 2001, Rivers Cuomo intentionally leaked an unofficial album online. This included at least four recording sessions from rehearsals featuring 18 new songs, and about two dozen more recorded live during the Warp Tour using an eight-track mobile unit. "They were also part of an unofficial album that was intentionally leaked online by Rivers in 2001."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Vocalizing Guitar Solos
xref.body: As part of his songwriting process, Rivers Cuomo would first sound out guitar solos vocally. This technique allowed him to develop the melodic contours of solos before translating them to the instrument. "Guitar solos were sounded out vocally first."
